svg.aria-label: One dense transformer layer with the four places model families diverge marked: the q k v projection widths and their optional bias, a per-head q and k normalization that only some families have, and a tied output embedding at the end of the model. The per-head normalization costs the fused qkv+rope decode path, because it sits between two operations that the fused kernel performs in one pass.
svg.text: ONE DENSE LAYER, AND THE FOUR PLACES FAMILIES DIVERGE
read top to bottom; the dashed box exists in one family and not the other
pre-norm (rms_norm)
q / k / v projections
per-head q/k norm
rope
attention
output projection
residual add
ffn gate / up, silu x, down
residual add
final norm, vocab matmul
1) widths: q is n_head x head_dim, k/v are n_head_kv x head_dim.
head_dim comes from metadata when a family decouples it; k/v also carry
an optional bias that one family reads and another does not have at all.
2) an op between two fused ones: this is the expensive difference. The
fused decode kernel does bias + rope + store in one pass and cannot
express a norm in between, so the family that needs it loses the fusion.
3) the rope table: the base and the frequency scale come from metadata,
one family adds per-pair scaling factors, and the table's width follows
head_dim - so a wrong head width corrupts positions, not shapes.
4) tied output: when the file has no output weight, the embedding is
reused. A loader rule, not a graph shape - and the one a copy forgets.
what a family owns: shapes, flags, a stop set. What it does not own: the vocabulary, the allocator, the scheduler, the fusion pass.
